posts.content:
OpenSSL: Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)

OpenSSL 기여자 nmouha가 `EVP_EncodeBlock()`의 버퍼 오버플로를 CVE-2026-121481로 보고하고, 잘못된 입력을 검사하는 패치를 제안했다. 제안은 NULL 버퍼, 음수 길이, 인코딩 결과가 `int`에 담기지 않는 길이에서 오류를 반환하고, `EVP_DecodeBlock()` 및 `http_client.c`의 Base64 길이 검사도 보완하며 테스트와 문서를 추가한다. 보고자는 환경 변수로 매우 큰 `-proxy_pass`를 전달한 `openssl s_client`에서 재현 가능하다고 했지만, 자문은 아직 공개되지 않았고 일부 유지관리...

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/33652

OpenSSL heap buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() output sizing

OpenSSL은 CVE-2026-121481로, EVP_EncodeBlock()의 출력 크기 계산이 정수 범위를 넘을 때 호출자 버퍼 뒤에 데이터를 쓰는 힙 버퍼 오버플로를 수정했다. 영향 범위는 OpenSSL 4.0.0~4.0.3 및 4.1.0이며, 각각 4.0.4와 4.1.1에서 고쳐졌다. 문제는 인코딩된 크기가 int에 담기지 않을 정도로 큰, 약 1.5GB 이상의 입력을 처리할 때 발생할 수 있다. 네트워크 접근만으로 악용 가능한 것으로 평가됐지만, CISA KEV 등재와 공개 익스플로잇은 확인되지 않았고 기본 구성의 노출 여부도 불분명하다.

https://cve.now/CVE-2026-121481

#openssl #cve #bufferoverflow #security #base64

A critical pam-mysql authentication bypass (CVE-2026-124749) lets remote attackers log in via SSH. Read our pam-mysql authentication bypass 2026 guide.

#Linux #pam_mysql #OpenSSH #CyberSecurity #CVE2026124749 #InfoSec

https://securityonline.info/pam-mysql-authentication-bypass-cve-2026-124749/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

🚨 BREAKING: A CRITICAL LINUX AUTHENTICATION FLAW LETS ATTACKERS LOG IN TO SSH SERVERS USING ANY PASSWORD.

Tracked as CVE-2026-124749, the vulnerability affects pam-mysql, a PAM module used to authenticate Linux and BSD users against MySQL databases. The researcher rates it CVSS 9.8. The alarming part? A single inverted boolean flag causes pam-mysql to accept ANY non-empty password for accounts whose database password is SQL NULL, even when OpenSSH is configured to reject passwordless logins by default.

Every released version of pam-mysql is affected, including the 0.8.x series and 1.0.0 betas. The issue can also affect other services relying on the same PAM module. Debian security fixes are available, but upstream has yet to publish a tagged release containing the patch.

Here's how a one-character logic error turned a security restriction into an authentication bypass, which configurations are exposed and how to fix it ↓
https://thecybersecguru.com/exploits/cve-2026-124749-pam-mysql-authentication-bypass/

posts.content: @rf New ruby2shell CVE-2026-132825, Mastodon servers for example=)

RT: @MosheTov Ruby2Shell is out: nothingburger, or actual issue?

Ruby2Shell (CVE-2026-132825) is a real bug, a one-byte heap overflow in Ruby’s string case conversion, but nothing published so far shows it can be turned into a reliable attack on real-world applications: there’s no exploitation in the wild, no weaponized exploit, narrow preconditions, and a 7.4 (High) rating rather than Critical. Our verdict is that it’s mostly trend, so upgrade to Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14 at a reasonable pace, starting with internet-facing apps that pass untrusted input to regex or case conversion, and skip the weekend war room.

Experts recommend updating LiteLLM and Starlette…

https://en.hacks.gr/aytomatopoiimenes-epitheseis-stocheyoyn-ektetheimena-systimata-toy-litellm/

#LiteLLM #Starlette #CVE_2026_42271 #CVE_2026_48710

CVE-2026-48710.description: Starlette is a lightweight ASGI framework/toolkit. Prior to version 1.0.1, the HTTP `Host` request header was not validated before being used to reconstruct `request.url`. Because the routing algorithm relies on the raw HTTP path while `request.url` is rebuilt from the `Host` header, a malformed header could make `request.url.path` differ from the path that was actually requested. Middleware and endpoints that apply security restrictions based on `request.url` (rather than the raw `scope` path) could therefore be bypassed. Users should upgrade to a version greater than or equal to version 1.0.1, which validates the `Host` header against the grammar of RFC 9112 §3.2 / RFC 3986 §3.2.2 when constructing `request.url` and falls back to `scope["server"]` for malformed values.

CVE-2026-42271.description: LiteLLM is a proxy server (AI Gateway) to call LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format. From version 1.74.2 to before version 1.83.7, two endpoints used to preview an MCP server before saving it — POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list — accepted a full server configuration in the request body, including the command, args, and env fields used by the stdio transport. When called with a stdio configuration, the endpoints attempted to connect, which spawned the supplied command as a subprocess on the proxy host with the privileges of the proxy process. The endpoints were gated only by a valid proxy API key, with no role check. Any authenticated user — including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys — could therefore run arbitrary commands on the host. This issue has been patched in version 1.83.7.

CVE-2026-133577.description: A flaw was found in the Kuadrant WebAssembly (WASM) shim shipped in Red Hat Connectivity Link 1.5. When a TokenRateLimitPolicy is attached to an HTTPRoute that also has an AuthPolicy - or when a RateLimitPolicy with defaults or overrides is attached to the Gateway or listener of such routes - the shim's action pipeline fails to dispatch the authentication guard at request time, and the request is forwarded upstream. Unauthenticated requests return 200 OK instead of 401, and neither authentication nor rate limiting is enforced. Both policies continue to report Enforced, leaving no status-level indication of the failure.

posts.content:
VMware und KVM: Neue Sicherheitslücken im Überblick

VMware hat zwei Sicherheitshinweise mit jeweils einem CVSS-Wert von 9,8 veröffentlicht, die vCenter und Apache betreffen. Parallel wurde in Linux KVM die Schwachstelle CVE-2026-99312 bekannt. Sie trifft AMD-Systeme mit verschachtelter Virtualisierung und lässt sich per Konfiguration umgehen.

https://www.all-about-security.de/vmware-und-kvm-neue-sicherheitsluecken-im-ueberblick/

#sicherheitslucken #sicherheitsupdate #vmware

CVE-2026-99312.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already
disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while
L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU
context.

Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled
or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role.  Even though
it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active,
there's zero value in not handling SMM.  At that point, the only scenario
where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the
vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those
modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the
MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides
most of the re-configuration in that case).

Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an
unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while
L2 is active.

Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even
though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT
events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when
CR0.PG must be '0').

CVE-2026-123007.description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.
